newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan ambassador to Peru an aid, research expert.
newsitem.headline: Japan ambassador to Peru an aid, research expert.

text.p: The Japanese ambassador to Peru now being held hostage by guerrillas at his residence in Lima is a seasoned diplomat and well versed in international aid and research affairs, according to the Foreign Ministry.
Morihisa Aoki, 58, was a senior official of the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), the aid arm of the Foreign Ministry, before he was named ambassador to Peru in 1994.
He has also served as a deputy foreign minister and chief of the ministry's intelligence and research bureau.

After passing the senior civil servants exam in 1962 from the elite Tokyo University, he joined the Foreign Ministry in 1963 and served at the Japanese embassies in the Philippines, Hong Kong and the United Nations.
Aoki's wife Naoko was with him at the reception when the guerrillas attacked but it was not clear if she had been freed. The couple have a son, but he is in Japan, the ministry said.
